subject.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings

question: Should Feishu conversation binding use explicit peer syntax, channel-specific Feishu ID inference, or a different compatibility plan for the existing `--bind <channel>:<account>` CLI contract?
rationale: The PR fixes a real routing gap, but it changes a documented CLI grammar that writes persisted config and several open candidate PRs make different compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Preserve account syntax and add explicit peer syntax
options.body: Keep `feishu:<account>` as an account bind and add a documented peer form such as `feishu:group:<id>` or another explicit conversation syntax.

options.title: Adopt Feishu ID inference with safeguards
options.body: Recognize known Feishu conversation IDs as peers while preserving unrecognized account names as account bindings and documenting the heuristic.

options.title: Pause this branch and choose another candidate
options.body: Close or pause this PR if another open candidate better preserves compatibility and can supply stronger proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve account syntax and add explicit peer syntax
recommendation.body: Keep `feishu:<account>` as an account bind and add a documented peer form such as `feishu:group:<id>` or another explicit conversation syntax.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has history on the multi-agent routing model and public agent CLI docs, which makes him the best available owner for the bind grammar decision.
